name: Tiptap
heroTitle: Comments and co-editing, built for Tiptap
heroSecondary: Add comments and co-editing, plus live presence, to your Tiptap editor, for your users and your AI agents. Threads stay pinned to the content as the document changes, and every agent edit lands as a suggestion your users approve, so a comment on paragraph three is still on paragraph three after a rewrite.
problemHeader: Build this into Tiptap yourself, and you rebuild it on every release.
problemBody: Your users expect to comment and co-edit in Tiptap, and your AI agents need that same editor with a human approving before they touch user work. Comments that survive Tiptap's transactions are a multi-quarter build, and the moment anchoring breaks, feedback lands on the wrong line. Co-editing is the harder half: rolled by hand, it means overwrites, lost work, and merge conflicts, the "my changes disappeared" bug reports, plus a websocket fleet and offline merge to keep alive. And the harder question is your agents: a useful agent needs to change the work, but an agent with write access to user content is what your buyers' security review blocks, so without a consent step, you choose between an agent that is useful and an agent that is safe. Every quarter spent on this is a quarter not spent on your own product.
builtForLine: Velt is the review and collaboration layer built for Tiptap: your users and your AI agents work the same editor, with comment threads anchored to each node, and every agent suggestion is a change a human approves before it lands.

problemHeader: Build this into Nivo yourself, and you rebuild it on every release.
problemBody: Your users expect to comment and co-edit in Nivo, and your AI agents need that same chart with a human approving before they touch user work. Comments that survive Nivo's re-renders are a multi-quarter build, and the moment anchoring breaks, feedback lands on the wrong data point. Co-editing is the harder half: rolled by hand, it means overwrites, lost work, and merge conflicts, the "my changes disappeared" bug reports, plus a websocket fleet and offline merge to keep alive. And the harder question is your agents: a useful agent needs to change the work, but an agent with write access to user content is what your buyers' security review blocks, so without a consent step, you choose between an agent that is useful and an agent that is safe. Every quarter spent on this is a quarter not spent on your own product.
